neighbours.label: the subject that opens a personal anecdote ('A friend said...', 'When I decided...'), as against the same nouns in generic or instructional statements
fire: I teach piano on weekends. A student asked me yesterday whether scales really matter.
Our shop opened in May. A customer wrote to me recently about a missing parcel.
It was a long shift at the pharmacy. A patient came in just before closing, very upset.
Last summer was strange. When I agreed to coach the team, I had never played the sport.
My book club meets monthly. A friend suggested last week that we read poetry instead.
The seminar ran late again. A colleague told me afterwards that she had nearly left.
I have kept bees for years. When I started, a neighbour lent me his old hive.
We run a small inn by the coast. A guest once left us a painting as a thank-you.
quiet: Every order is checked twice. Students who enrol early pay a reduced fee each term.
Our shop opens at nine. Customers must keep their receipt for any return.
Follow the leaflet closely. Each patient should drink plenty of water after surgery.
Training starts in May. Coaches are required to hold a first-aid certificate.
Book clubs vary in size. Friends of the library receive a monthly newsletter.
The seminar runs weekly. Colleagues from other departments are welcome to attend.
Beekeeping takes patience. Neighbours of an apiary rarely notice the bees at all.
Inns along the coast fill up fast. Guests can check in from three o'clock.
